books.section: Topic 4.8 Jackson and Federal Power, A. The Second Two-Party System: The Democrats and the Whigs
The Whig Party and the Second Party System
The Jackson Presidency and Jacksonian Democracy

stimulus.text: The campaign lithograph, published in 1840, shows General William Henry Harrison in military uniform with a sword, under the words 'GENERAL WM. H. HARRISON.' A wreath names his victories: 'Tippecanoe, Fort Meigs and the Thames.' The Whigs campaigned for Harrison with the slogan 'Tippecanoe and Tyler Too' and with log cabins and hard cider as symbols.
stimulus.source_note: Lithograph 'General Wm. H. Harrison of Tippecanoe, Fort Meigs and the Thames,' published 1840 (Library of Congress). Public domain; image viewed before writing.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note
stem: Harrison won the election of 1840 but died a month after taking office. What was the most important consequence for the Whig Party?

options.text: The Whigs won every presidential election for the next twenty years
options.misconception: A landslide win feels like the start of an era, so it is easy to stretch it across the next twenty years.

options.text: Tyler, a states'-rights man, vetoed the Whigs' bank bills
The Democrats immediately repealed the protective tariff
options.misconception: A new president often reverses the old tariff, so it is easy to think the Democrats repealed it at once.
A president dying in office sounds like a constitutional crisis, so it is easy to imagine the office itself was abolished.

rationales.A: The Whigs won only once more, in 1848, and the party broke apart in the 1850s over slavery.
rationales.B: Vice President John Tyler, a former Democrat who favored states' rights, vetoed the Whig program for a national bank, and his cabinet resigned in protest.
rationales.C: The tariff was raised, not repealed, by the Tariff of 1842, two years after Harrison's death.
rationales.D: Congress never abolished the presidency; Tyler simply took the oath and served out Harrison's term.
rationales.general:
1. Name the successor. Vice President John Tyler, a Virginian and former Democrat, took the oath in April 1841.
2. Ask what Tyler believed. He favored states' rights, so he vetoed the Whigs' bills for a new national bank.
Background: the vetoes drove Tyler from the party, and his whole cabinet except one man resigned.
Remember: a vice president is a bet on the future — ask what happens when the pick disagrees with the party.
